note: The eight parts of the series « Préparer sa première Omra » (spec: series premiere-omra, 8 parts, track omra, master_locale fr, pillar /guide-omra, commercial_intent guide, spacing 6–9 days). One reader, one journey: the decision, the agency and the contract, the file, the timing, the tier, the body and the bag, the rites, the departure day. Every part is evergreen (no hijri anchor, no window), owns a long-tail first-timer question that no guide page owns, names its closest existing URL and how it differs, and pushes every volatile fact — prices, dates, seats, hotel distances, deposit terms — into a live component. The seven guide chapters remain the owners of « documents et visa », « meilleure période », « budget », « checklist », « rituels », « femme et mahram » : these parts link up to them and never re-target their queries. Written on 2026-09-15.

topics.angle: Part 5: the tier and the room. What separates one grade from another in practice — the standing of the hotel, how long the walk to the Haram takes at a crowded hour, whether a room is shared by two people or by four — and how those two decisions, more than anything else on the programme, move what each traveller pays. Hotel cards render the partner properties with their real distance; the prose carries neither a metre nor a dirham, only what the difference feels like at three in the morning.
topics.delta: That post describes the tiers from economy to VIP as a catalogue. This part is the first-timer's decision between two variables that interact: proximity and room occupancy. It explains the arbitration (a nearer hotel shared with three people, or a further one in a double), shows real partner hotels through their cards rather than describing them, and links the tier post and the budget chapter for the rest.

topics.angle: Part 8 closes the series with the day itself. Meeting the group at Mohammed V and what the team handles there, the flight and the moment ihram is taken, arrival and the transfer, the first sight of the Haram and how a first Omra usually unfolds in those opening hours, then the move between the two cities and the return — the habits worth keeping, what to do with the emotion of the first days back, and how a second departure gets decided later. Points back to the pillar guide as the reference for everything the series covered.
topics.delta: That post handles what goes WRONG on site — a lost passport, illness, getting separated. This part narrates what normally happens: the assembly at the airport, the flight and the ihram, the arrival, the first hours at the Haram, the two cities and the return home. It links the unexpected-events post for the incidents rather than covering them, and closes the eight-part arc.
